verdict.rationale: mParticle's Data Privacy Controls docs say consent state drives both GDPR consent and CCPA data-sale opt-out. Forwarding rules can then block data to destinations, for example "Do not forward if CCPA Data sale opt out is present", and a Consent Filters guide exists. That is direct, first-party support for capturing consent and enforcing it downstream. However, the evidence leaves parts of the story thin: per-category (GDPR purpose) enforcement is not described in depth, and enforcement appears to depend on configured forwarding rules rather than being proven automatic across all destinations. missing for 10: documented detail on granular consent-category filtering per destination, documentation of how consent is captured via SDK/API, evidence that enforcement applies automatically across every downstream integration, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a privacy lead, user consent is captured and enforced across destinations — opt-outs and consent categories are honored downstream automatically

citations.quote: Manage your consent and opt-out privacy obligations under the GDPR and CCPA with Data Privacy Controls
Consent state powers both GDPR consent and CCPA data sale opt-out
Applying a forwarding rule of: Do not forward if CCPA Data sale opt out is present.
